name: Amasa
description: Ishmaelite living at the time of United Monarchy

points: David told Amasa to assemble the men of Judah within three days, but Amasa tarried longer than the set time. So David sent Abishai with Joab's men, the Cherethites, the Pelethites, and all the mighty men to pursue Sheba lest he escape into fenced cities.

At the great stone in Gibeon, Joab came to Amasa with a sword secretly fastened, took him by the beard with his right hand as if to kiss him, and smote him in the fifth rib so that his bowels shed to the ground, and he died at one stroke. Joab was grimy and shady, murdering the man who had been named captain in his place.

One of Joab's men stood by Amasa calling all who favored Joab and David to follow after Joab. Amasa wallowed in his blood in the midst of the highway, and when the people stood still to look, the man removed him into the field and cast a cloth over him, and then all the people went on after Joab to pursue Sheba.

Joab, who had turned after Adonijah, flees to the tabernacle of the Lord and catches hold of the horns of the altar, but Solomon sends Benaiah to fall upon him. Joab dies for the innocent blood he shed when he slew Abner and Amasa, two men more righteous and better than he, without David's knowledge.

note.label: 1 Kings 2: The Charge to Solomon and the Kingdom Established
